decisions.final_value: Rate at which an identified carrier gas is supplied through the specified process boundary, expressed on a declared volumetric, amount-of-substance, or mass basis.
decisions.rationale: The replacement defines a flow-rate family while retaining the physical basis required for each value.
decisions.implementation: Use quantity-kind subclasses or an explicit basis field. For volumetric flow, state actual or standard reference temperature and pressure; do not mix flow rate with gas velocity.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst and ionomer to peg ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Combined dry mass of catalyst material and ionomer divided by the mass of polyethylene glycol additive used in the same formulation.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst and ionomer to peg ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The components and ratio direction are clear, but the source does not explicitly establish the mass basis.
decisions.implementation: Confirm the source recipe uses a mass ratio before adopting this definition. Identify the catalyst material and dry ionomer mass; exclude dispersion solvent. If a different basis was used, preserve it as a separately defined ratio.

decisions.current_value: A morphological characteristic that represents catalyst layer tortuosity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of a specified mean connected path length through the catalyst-layer pore network to the straight through-layer distance in the selected direction.
decisions.final_value: Ratio of a specified mean connected path length through the catalyst-layer pore network to the straight through-layer distance in the selected direction.
decisions.rationale: The geometric-tortuosity aliases support a path-length ratio rather than a transport tortuosity factor.
decisions.implementation: Specify path-selection and averaging rules. Do not substitute the square of this ratio or a factor inferred from effective diffusivity; retain those as separately defined transport quantities.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of an explicitly identified catalyst component deposited in an electrode divided by the geometric electrode area carrying that component.
decisions.final_value: Mass of an explicitly identified catalyst component deposited in an electrode divided by the geometric electrode area carrying that component.
decisions.rationale: This specifies the areal basis while keeping metal mass and total supported-catalyst mass distinguishable.
decisions.implementation: Identify numerator material for every value. Platinum-only loading and total Pt/C powder loading require separate quantity records or subclasses; a generic catalyst-loading parent may group them.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst loading pattern for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Categorical description of the spatial arrangement of deposited catalyst within an electrode, including a continuous full-area coating or a specified arrangement of coated and uncoated segments.
decisions.final_value: Categorical description of the spatial arrangement of deposited catalyst within an electrode, including a continuous full-area coating or a specified arrangement of coated and uncoated segments.
decisions.rationale: The source pattern examples describe spatial categories rather than a constituent amount.
decisions.implementation: Describe segment positions and hydrophilic/hydrophobic treatment where applicable; represent numeric local loading separately.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic representing Catalyst Mass in the H2KG domain model.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of the identified catalyst material used as a specimen quantity or normalization basis, excluding separately added ionomer and solvent unless these are explicitly part of the identified material.
decisions.final_value: Mass of the identified catalyst material used as a specimen quantity or normalization basis, excluding separately added ionomer and solvent unless these are explicitly part of the identified material.
decisions.rationale: The replacement identifies the material boundary without treating metal-only mass as synonymous with total supported-powder mass.
decisions.implementation: A generic catalyst-mass class can remain broad. Identify the catalyst material in the value record; split metal-only and total supported-catalyst bases when homogeneous normalization is required. The Pt-mass alias issue is separate from definition acceptance.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst mass concentration in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of the identified dry catalyst material divided by the final volume of the prepared catalyst ink.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst mass concentration in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Standard mass concentration uses final mixture volume, whereas the description states catalyst mass per solvent volume.  References 17.
decisions.implementation: Use this definition only for records based on final ink volume. For the stated mg/mL of solvent convention, use the alternative and rename the quantity Catalyst mass per added solvent volume; existing values must not be silently reassigned between the two bases.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst suspension concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of the identified dry catalyst material divided by the final volume of its suspension.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst suspension concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: A heterogeneous catalyst suspension is commonly characterized on a mass-per-volume basis, but this source does not fix the concentration kind.  References 17.
decisions.implementation: Confirm the source uses mass concentration before adopting. A particle-number concentration or amount concentration must be defined separately; identify the catalyst and final suspension medium.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst to nafion weight ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Dry mass of the catalyst material, including any additives that the source explicitly groups with it, divided by the dry mass of Nafion polymer in the same formulation.
decisions.final_value: Dry mass of the catalyst material, including any additives that the source explicitly groups with it, divided by the dry mass of Nafion polymer in the same formulation.
decisions.rationale: The replacement fixes the stated catalyst-to-ionomer direction and excludes dispersion solvent from the polymer mass.
decisions.implementation: Identify which solids are counted as catalyst in the CoTMPP-based recipe. Nafion-to-carbon ratio and its abbreviation N/C are different quantities and should be removed as synonyms of this class.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst weight percent in oil for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of catalyst added to the reaction divided by the initial oil mass and multiplied by 100.
decisions.final_value: Mass of catalyst added to the reaction divided by the initial oil mass and multiplied by 100.
decisions.rationale: The description explicitly uses oil mass as the reference; this is an additive-to-feed mass percentage rather than catalyst mass fraction of the final mixture.
decisions.implementation: Rename the preferred label to Catalyst-to-oil mass percentage or Catalyst dosage relative to oil mass. If any records instead use catalyst divided by catalyst plus oil mass, keep them as a separate total-mixture mass fraction.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents cathode catalyst loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of the specified catalyst material in the cathode divided by the geometric electrode area over which that material is deposited.
decisions.final_value: Mass of the specified catalyst material in the cathode divided by the geometric electrode area over which that material is deposited.
decisions.rationale: The replacement defines the area normalization without treating catalytic-metal mass and whole supported-powder mass as identical.
decisions.implementation: Identify the numerator in each record, for example platinum mass, palladium mass, or total supported-catalyst powder mass. If homogeneous quantities are needed, represent these as distinct subclasses; do not change historical metal loadings into powder loadings.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents cathode mpl carbon support loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of carbon material in the cathode microporous layer divided by the geometric area coated by that microporous layer.
decisions.final_value: Mass of carbon material in the cathode microporous layer divided by the geometric area coated by that microporous layer.
decisions.rationale: The areal carbon loading requires the carbon numerator and coated-area denominator.
decisions.implementation: Exclude binder and other noncarbon constituents from the numerator; identify the actual MPL carbon material.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents cathode stoichiometric ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of the molar oxygen supply rate to the cathode to the stoichiometric oxygen-consumption rate corresponding to the operating current; for a single hydrogen fuel cell the latter is I/(4F).
decisions.final_value: Ratio of the molar oxygen supply rate to the cathode to the stoichiometric oxygen-consumption rate corresponding to the operating current; for a single hydrogen fuel cell the latter is I/(4F).
decisions.rationale: The quantity compares reactant supply with reaction demand; it is not oxygen fraction in the feed.
decisions.implementation: I is cell current and F is the Faraday constant. For air feed, calculate supplied oxygen from the air flow and its oxygen composition. State per-cell versus stack boundary and any reference-current convention at zero current.

decisions.current_value: A density characteristic that represents cell seeding density for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Initial number of biological cells seeded onto a culture substrate divided by the seeded substrate area.
decisions.final_value: A density characteristic that represents cell seeding density for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Surface seeding density and suspension cell concentration have different dimensional bases.
decisions.implementation: Use this definition for cells-per-area records. If the source reports cells per suspension volume, use the alternative as a separately labelled cell-seeding number concentration.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting xPS-derived surface oxidation-state ratio for Co.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of the estimated surface abundance of cobalt in oxidation state +2 to that in oxidation state +3, obtained from a declared X-ray photoelectron-spectroscopy peak-fitting model.
decisions.final_value: Ratio of the estimated surface abundance of cobalt in oxidation state +2 to that in oxidation state +3, obtained from a declared X-ray photoelectron-spectroscopy peak-fitting model.
decisions.rationale: The Co2+/Co3+ alias identifies the ratio direction that was absent from the primary definition.
decisions.implementation: State the fitted spectral components and correction convention. Treat the result as an XPS-derived surface estimate rather than an unqualified bulk stoichiometric ratio.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents coagulating agent mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of the coagulating additive divided by the total dry mass of all formulation solids, including that additive.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents coagulating agent mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The dry-solids basis must be distinguished from a wet-ink fraction and from additive mass relative to pre-existing solids.  References 18.
decisions.implementation: Confirm whether the source includes PEI in total dry solids. If the denominator excludes the additive, use the alternative and label it Coagulating-agent-to-base-solids mass ratio.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting constrictivity derived from reconstructed pore-network bottlenecks in FIBSEM Tomography Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Dimensionless descriptor of the restriction imposed by variations in pore cross-section, particularly constrictions connecting larger pore bodies, evaluated using a declared pore-network or transport model.
decisions.final_value: Dimensionless descriptor of the restriction imposed by variations in pore cross-section, particularly constrictions connecting larger pore bodies, evaluated using a declared pore-network or transport model.
decisions.rationale: This captures the physical concept without choosing among non-equivalent numerical constrictivity formulae.
decisions.implementation: Attach the actual equation and direction to each source-specific calculation. Do not interchange throat-to-body size ratios, squared ratios, or transport-based factors; create method-specific subclasses when numerical interoperability requires one formula.

decisions.current_value: A density characteristic that represents co stripping specific charge density for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Reference oxidation charge per unit real platinum surface area assigned to removal of a specified adsorbed carbon-monoxide coverage during CO-stripping voltammetry, used to convert integrated stripping charge to electrochemically active platinum area.
decisions.final_value: Reference oxidation charge per unit real platinum surface area assigned to removal of a specified adsorbed carbon-monoxide coverage during CO-stripping voltammetry, used to convert integrated stripping charge to electrochemically active platinum area.
decisions.rationale: The calibration-charge alias supports a reference charge density rather than measured stripping charge per geometric area.
decisions.implementation: State assumed CO coverage, catalyst surface, background treatment, and the adopted calibration value and unit. Do not insert a universal numerical value for all catalysts or adsorption protocols.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting CPE admittance Y 0 and determined in Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Potentiostatic and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Galvanostatic.
decisions.recommended_value: The frequency-independent coefficient multiplying the nth power of imaginary angular frequency in the admittance of a specified constant-phase element, where n is the element's dimensionless exponent.
decisions.final_value: The frequency-independent coefficient multiplying the nth power of imaginary angular frequency in the admittance of a specified constant-phase element, where n is the element's dimensionless exponent.
decisions.rationale: Y0 is an admittance prefactor, not generally an ordinary conductance or capacitance.  References 34.
decisions.implementation: For omega in rad/s and unnormalized admittance in siemens, Y0 has units S s^n. Record n and whether the fitted element is normalized to area; Y0 equals capacitance only when n = 1.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting crack aspect ratio and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of a crack’s characteristic length to its characteristic width, using declared length and width extraction methods.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting crack aspect ratio and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.
decisions.rationale: A crack shape ratio is geometric, and its orientation must be stated to distinguish it from a reciprocal width-to-length ratio.
decisions.implementation: Confirm the source uses length/width. If it uses aperture/length, depth/width, or another convention, replace the dimensions in the definition and retain that source-specific label.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents crack connectivity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Fraction of detected catalyst-layer cracks that span the complete layer thickness from one bounding interface to the other, calculated as the number of spanning cracks divided by the total number of detected cracks.
decisions.final_value: Fraction of detected catalyst-layer cracks that span the complete layer thickness from one bounding interface to the other, calculated as the number of spanning cracks divided by the total number of detected cracks.
decisions.rationale: The description identifies a through-penetrating-crack count fraction rather than an unspecified connectivity metric.
decisions.implementation: Report as a fraction or percentage and state segmentation, connected-component, and crack-counting rules; record which interfaces define the layer thickness.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting crack density and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Number of individually identified cracks divided by the inspected specimen surface area.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting crack density and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.
decisions.rationale: Crack count per area, total crack length per area, and cracked-area fraction are distinct measures; the original does not identify one.
decisions.implementation: Use this replacement only after confirming the source uses count per area. If it reports total crack length per area, use the first alternative and label Crack length density. If it reports area fraction, use the second alternative and label Crack area fraction.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack volume accessibility at 20 um for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Fraction of the total segmented crack volume that a spherical probe of 20 micrometres diameter can reach from the membrane/catalyst-layer interface without intersecting the solid phase, under the stated simulated-intrusion algorithm.
decisions.final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack volume accessibility at 20 um for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The source identifies probe-based accessible crack volume, but not whether 20 micrometres is the diameter or radius.
decisions.implementation: Confirm probe diameter before using this definition. If the source defines a 20-micrometre radius, use the alternative. State whether the algorithm includes the full intruded volume or only sphere-centre-accessible volume.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack width d 50 cwd for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Median of the crack-width distribution obtained by the declared crack-width-distribution image-analysis method, that is, the width at cumulative distribution fraction 0.5.
decisions.final_value: Median of the crack-width distribution obtained by the declared crack-width-distribution image-analysis method, that is, the width at cumulative distribution fraction 0.5.
decisions.rationale: D50 is a percentile, not a mean; its method and distribution basis must be retained.
decisions.implementation: State whether the cumulative distribution is number-, length-, area-, or volume-weighted and how local width is extracted. Remove mean crack width as a synonym unless the source itself incorrectly used that wording; preserve such source wording in provenance rather than the preferred scientific label.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack width d 50 mip for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Median equivalent crack-entry size in the cumulative distribution generated by the declared simulated mercury-intrusion analysis, corresponding to cumulative fraction 0.5.
decisions.final_value: Median equivalent crack-entry size in the cumulative distribution generated by the declared simulated mercury-intrusion analysis, corresponding to cumulative fraction 0.5.
decisions.rationale: Intrusion-derived sizes are controlled by access constrictions and need not equal local geometric crack widths.
decisions.implementation: State the size convention (diameter, radius, or aperture), cumulative weighting, interface of intrusion, and intrusion algorithm. Do not replace a source diameter with a radius or assume volume weighting without checking the source.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents degree of sulfonation for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Average number of sulfonic-acid groups, including their ionized forms, attached per polymer repeat unit of an explicitly specified repeat-unit composition.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents degree of sulfonation for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: A group-per-repeat-unit degree must be distinguished from the fraction of available substitution sites that are occupied.
decisions.implementation: For the stated sPEEK context, confirm the repeat-unit and proton-NMR integration convention. If the source defines a percentage of sulfonated sites instead, use the alternative with a site-based label and do not identify it numerically with groups per repeat unit without the conversion.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents deposition rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Volume of ink deposited onto or into the target structure per unit time during the specified printing process.
decisions.final_value: VolumetricInkDepositionRate
decisions.rationale: The description explicitly identifies a volumetric printing rate.
decisions.implementation: Distinguish delivered volume from nominal syringe flow if losses or draw-out occur. Do not combine thickness-growth rate or deposited mass per time under this definition.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents direct ink writing 2 for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents direct ink writing 2 for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: This is an unresolved placeholder with no recoverable physical quantity.
decisions.implementation: Trace the original extracted field and source. If it represents a process, reuse the existing DirectInkWriting process class; if it represents a setting, recover its true name, quantity, and definition. Do not create a numerical definition or reclassify a setting as a process merely from the placeholder label.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents dispersant mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of dispersant divided by the total dry mass of all solids in the ceramic ink, including the dispersant.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents dispersant mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: A dry-total-solids fraction differs from dispersant dosage relative to the ceramic powder alone.  References 18.
decisions.implementation: Confirm the source denominator. If dispersant is added relative to powder mass excluding dispersant, use the alternative and rename it Dispersant-to-powder mass ratio.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents dmso mass fraction in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of dimethyl sulfoxide divided by the total mass of the catalyst ink, including solvent and solids.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents dmso mass fraction in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The existing class label denotes whole-ink fraction whereas the description denotes solvent-mixture fraction.  References 18.
decisions.implementation: Use this only for total-ink mass fractions. If the reported 5 wt.% refers to the solvent mixture, use the alternative and rename the class DMSO mass fraction in solvent mixture. Confirm whether 5 wt.% denotes a fraction of the final mixture or an addition relative to an initial solvent amount.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting durability with cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Elapsed operating time under a specified cycling protocol until a declared performance-loss or failure criterion is reached.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting durability with cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.
decisions.rationale: Durability expressed as time requires an endpoint; mere test exposure is not automatically a measured lifetime.
decisions.implementation: State the cycling conditions, performance observable, baseline, and loss threshold. If the reported value is simply completed exposure without reaching an endpoint, use the alternative, rename it Cycling test duration, and record that the durability endpoint was not reached.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting durability without cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Elapsed operating time under a specified noncycling protocol until a declared performance-loss or failure criterion is reached.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting durability without cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.
decisions.rationale: Durability expressed as time requires an endpoint; mere test exposure is not automatically a measured lifetime.
decisions.implementation: State the noncycling conditions, performance observable, baseline, and loss threshold. If the reported value is simply completed exposure without reaching an endpoint, use the alternative, rename it Noncycling test duration, and record that the durability endpoint was not reached.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents dye concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of the identified dye divided by the volume of the prepared test solution.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents dye concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Dye concentration may be reported on mass or amount basis; the previous primary definition identified neither.  References 14, 17.
decisions.implementation: Use this definition for mass/volume records. For molar records use the alternative as a separate amount-concentration subclass. Identify Rhodamine B, methylene blue, or another actual dye and initial versus time-dependent state; these dye names are not synonyms.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents eis perturbation amplitude for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Magnitude of the sinusoidal electrical perturbation used to measure electrochemical impedance about an operating point, with voltage or current and peak, peak-to-peak, or root-mean-square convention explicitly identified.
decisions.final_value: Magnitude of the sinusoidal electrical perturbation used to measure electrochemical impedance about an operating point, with voltage or current and peak, peak-to-peak, or root-mean-square convention explicitly identified.
decisions.rationale: This states the excitation quantity and convention while allowing a general EIS-amplitude concept.  References 34.
decisions.implementation: For the described 2 mV peak-to-peak record, preserve voltage and peak-to-peak qualifiers. Do not hard-code 2 mV as part of the class definition or make every historical amplitude peak-to-peak. Consider alignment or subclassing with ACAmplitude.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents electrical percolation threshold volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Critical volume fraction of the specified conductive phase at which a system-spanning electronically conducting network forms in the stated material model or experimental system.
decisions.final_value: Critical volume fraction of the specified conductive phase at which a system-spanning electronically conducting network forms in the stated material model or experimental system.
decisions.rationale: The threshold is a composition value marking onset of connectivity, rather than a geometrical extent.
decisions.implementation: Identify the conductive Pt/C phase, total-volume or solids-only denominator, transport direction, and fitted percolation equation. A finite experimental conductivity threshold must be reported with its criterion.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting electrochemically active surface area normalized to Catalyst Mass and Pt Mass and determined in Cyclic Voltammetry, ECSABy Double Layer Capacitance, and Carbon Monoxide Stripping Voltammetry.
decisions.recommended_value: Area of the catalyst surface that participates in a specified electrochemical probe reaction under the stated measurement conditions.
decisions.final_value: Area of the catalyst surface that participates in a specified electrochemical probe reaction under the stated measurement conditions.
decisions.rationale: Actual electrochemically active area and area normalized to platinum or total catalyst mass are distinct quantities.
decisions.implementation: Use area units for this unnormalized quantity. Keep Pt-mass-specific area and total-catalyst-mass-specific area distinct, with explicit normalization-basis records or separate quantity classes. Do not assign area-per-mass values to an unnormalized area quantity. Identify the probe, charge or capacitance calibration, and conditions because accessible area depends on the probe.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents electrolyte concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Composition characteristic expressing the quantity of an identified dissolved electrolyte species per unit volume of the final solution, with amount, mass, or another declared volume-based concentration kind specified.
decisions.final_value: Composition characteristic expressing the quantity of an identified dissolved electrolyte species per unit volume of the final solution, with amount, mass, or another declared volume-based concentration kind specified.
decisions.rationale: A broad concentration concept can remain general if its value records state the concentration kind; an arbitrary molar basis must not be invented.  References 14.
decisions.implementation: Use explicit subclasses or quantity-kind metadata for amount and mass concentration. Molality and mass fraction use different denominators and should be separately named. Identify analytical solute and avoid treating sulfuric acid, a generic dopant, and total ionic strength as the same observable.

decisions.current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents electron current for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Magnitude of electric charge carried by the electron beam per unit time during electron-microscopy or tomography acquisition.
decisions.final_value: Magnitude of electric charge carried by the electron beam per unit time during electron-microscopy or tomography acquisition.
decisions.rationale: Electron-beam current is an instrument setting rather than an intrinsic electrochemical-interface property.
decisions.implementation: Rename the preferred label to Electron beam current. Identify measured versus nominal probe current and acquisition mode as needed.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting electronic conductivity anisotropy ratio.
decisions.recommended_value: Electronic conductivity measured in the plane of a specimen divided by its electronic conductivity measured through the specimen thickness, for the same specimen state and measurement conditions.
decisions.final_value: Electronic conductivity measured in the plane of a specimen divided by its electronic conductivity measured through the specimen thickness, for the same specimen state and measurement conditions.
decisions.rationale: The IP/TP alias establishes the ratio direction; the replacement makes that direction explicit.
decisions.implementation: Record the selected in-plane direction if the plane itself is anisotropic. The reciprocal TP/IP ratio requires a separate convention.

decisions.current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents electrospinning applied voltage for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Electric potential applied to the electrospinning needle or spinneret relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.
decisions.final_value: Electric potential applied to the electrospinning needle or spinneret relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.
decisions.rationale: The source specifies needle voltage; it should not automatically be treated as the needle-to-collector potential difference when the collector is biased.
decisions.implementation: Record the reference, typically ground, and the collector potential. Compute needle-minus-collector voltage only from commensurate signed potentials. The process is electrohydrodynamic rather than intrinsically electrochemical.

decisions.current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents electrospinning collector voltage for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Electric potential of the electrospinning collector relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.
decisions.final_value: Electric potential of the electrospinning collector relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.
decisions.rationale: A collector electrostatic bias is not an electrochemical electrode potential.
decisions.implementation: State ground or another circuit reference and preserve the sign; do not describe the reference as an electrochemical reference electrode unless one is actually used.

decisions.current_value: A transport characteristic that represents electrospinning ink flow rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Volume of polymer-containing spinning ink supplied through the electrospinning nozzle per unit time.
decisions.final_value: A transport characteristic that represents electrospinning ink flow rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: This is the usual volumetric feed quantity, but the source record explicitly leaves its reported basis unresolved.
decisions.implementation: Confirm the source unit is volume/time before adopting. If it reports mass/time, use the alternative with a mass-flow label. Distinguish pump setting from measured jet throughput.

decisions.current_value: Equivalent radius representing the characteristic size of finite ionomer patches distributed over the secondary-pore surface.
decisions.recommended_value: Radius of a circular patch having the same surface area as the finite ionomer patch represented in the model; for patch area A, the area-equivalent radius is sqrt(A/pi).
decisions.final_value: Equivalent radius representing the characteristic size of finite ionomer patches distributed over the secondary-pore surface.
decisions.rationale: An equivalent radius requires a declared geometrical equivalence; the current definition does not specify one.
decisions.implementation: Use this replacement only if the model uses area-equivalent circular patches. Confirm whether A is actual covered surface area or a projected area and how multiple patches are averaged. If the source uses a hemisphere, volume equivalence, or another model radius, retain that exact construction instead.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents ethanol to water volume ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Volume of ethanol divided by volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture, with both component volumes measured before mixing under stated conditions.
decisions.final_value: Volume of ethanol divided by volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture, with both component volumes measured before mixing under stated conditions.
decisions.rationale: The quantity describes formulation composition and has an explicit ethanol-to-water direction.
decisions.implementation: This ratio differs from ethanol volume fraction; identify the pre-wetting solution or other mixture to which it applies.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents ethanol volume fraction in solvent mixture for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Volume of ethanol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.
decisions.final_value: Volume of ethanol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.
decisions.rationale: The numerator and solvent-only denominator define a constituent fraction rather than a geometric size.  References 12, 22.
decisions.implementation: Exclude non-solvent solids. If the source divides by final measured mixture volume, preserve that volume-concentration convention explicitly instead of silently treating it as the pre-mixing-volume fraction.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents ethylene glycol volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Volume of ethylene glycol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.
decisions.final_value: Volume of ethylene glycol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.
decisions.rationale: The supplied description identifies a solvent-mixture volume fraction.  References 12, 22.
decisions.implementation: Name the other solvents and exclude dissolved solids from the solvent-only denominator. Preserve a final-mixture-volume convention separately if that is what the source actually measured.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting external quantum efficiency and determined in Review Statement Extraction and External Quantum Efficiency Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of the number of charge carriers collected by a photoconverting device to the number of photons incident on the device, evaluated at the specified wavelength or over a declared spectral band.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting external quantum efficiency and determined in Review Statement Extraction and External Quantum Efficiency Measurement.
decisions.rationale: Photoconversion and light emission use opposite photon/carrier roles; the intended device type is not fixed by the current text.
decisions.implementation: Use this replacement only for the photon-to-charge measurement. For a light-emitting device use the alternative as a separate subclass. For photon-driven chemical reactions, define the counted product events or transferred charges explicitly rather than reuse a detector definition.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) content in biodiesel phase after reaction.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of fatty-acid methyl esters divided by the total mass of the analyzed biodiesel phase, expressed as a fraction or percentage.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) content in biodiesel phase after reaction.
decisions.rationale: A mass-based ester content differs from mole fraction and uncorrected chromatographic peak-area fraction.
decisions.implementation: Confirm the analytical method reports mass fraction before adopting. If only chromatographic area fraction is available, use the alternative and label it FAME chromatographic area fraction; do not convert it to mass content without a calibration.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents feed methane volume ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Methane gas volume divided by the total inlet-feed gas volume, with all volumes evaluated at the same temperature and pressure.
decisions.final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents feed methane volume ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The wording suggests a methane fraction but does not identify whether the denominator is total feed or another gas.
decisions.implementation: Use this definition and rename the preferred label Methane volume fraction in feed only if the denominator is total feed. If the source means methane-to-steam or methane-to-carbon-dioxide ratio, define that exact denominator in a distinct ratio class.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents feed rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Upward translational speed of the syringe or nozzle relative to the receiving substrate during formation of a printed pillar.
decisions.final_value: Upward translational speed of the syringe or nozzle relative to the receiving substrate during formation of a printed pillar.
decisions.rationale: The description denotes nozzle motion, whereas feed rate can also denote ink throughput.
decisions.implementation: Rename the preferred label to Nozzle withdrawal speed or Syringe withdrawal speed, according to the source apparatus. Remove ink feeding rate as a synonym; define volumetric ink delivery separately.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting estimated density of Fe–N4 sites from N 1s XPS fitting (assumption: 399.5 eV component originates from Fe–N4).
decisions.recommended_value: Estimated number of Fe–N4 coordination sites per unit dry catalyst mass, with each site comprising an iron centre coordinated to four nitrogen atoms.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting estimated density of Fe–N4 sites from N 1s XPS fitting (assumption: 399.5 eV component originates from Fe–N4).
decisions.rationale: An XPS component fraction alone does not supply an absolute site density without a conversion and normalization basis.
decisions.implementation: Use this mass-normalized definition only if supported by the source. State the conversion from fitted XPS intensity to site count, catalyst mass basis, and uncertainty. Retain the assignment of the 399.5 eV N 1s component to Fe–N4 as a source assumption, not a universal spectroscopic identity. For an area-normalized estimate, use the alternative.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ferritin analyte concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Amount of substance of the identified ferritin analyte divided by the final volume of the incubation solution used in the sensing assay.
decisions.final_value: Amount of substance of the identified ferritin analyte divided by the final volume of the incubation solution used in the sensing assay.
decisions.rationale: The picomolar context establishes an amount-concentration basis.  References 14.
decisions.implementation: State which ferritin molecular assembly the reported amount counts. Keep ferritin mass concentration separate; do not assume an unreported molecular mass for conversions.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ferritin template concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of ferritin used as the molecular-imprinting template divided by the volume of the template-containing precursor mixture.
decisions.final_value: Mass of ferritin used as the molecular-imprinting template divided by the volume of the template-containing precursor mixture.
decisions.rationale: The description identifies mass concentration, which is absent from the primary definition.
decisions.implementation: Record the precursor-mixture stage and volume reference conditions; do not substitute stock-solution concentration for final-mixture concentration.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents fiber ionomer to carbon ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of the dry mass of ionomer present as electrospun fibers to the mass of carbon support in the specified catalyst layer.
decisions.final_value: Ratio of the dry mass of ionomer present as electrospun fibers to the mass of carbon support in the specified catalyst layer.
decisions.rationale: The source description resolves the ratio as a mass ratio.
decisions.implementation: Keep fiber ionomer distinct from any additional nonfibrous ionomer; state which carbon-containing support is included.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents fiber ionomer volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Volume of the fiber-ionomer phase divided by the total volume of the specified catalyst-layer reference domain.
decisions.final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents fiber ionomer volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The original definition misclassifies the quantity and omits its denominator.  References 15.
decisions.implementation: Use this definition if the reference domain includes the full catalyst layer, including pores. If the source uses only solid phases, use the alternative and preserve that basis explicitly.

decisions.current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents fixed charge concentration in dry ionomer for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Amount of fixed ionic charge sites in an ionomer divided by the volume of the dry ionomer.
decisions.final_value: Amount of fixed ionic charge sites in an ionomer divided by the volume of the dry ionomer.
decisions.rationale: This is an amount concentration of ionic sites, not electrical charge per unit volume.
decisions.implementation: State the ionic-site species and ionomer acid or salt form. For multivalent sites, distinguish moles of sites from charge equivalents.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents flow field design for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Categorical characteristic identifying the arrangement and connectivity of flow channels in a flow field, such as parallel, serpentine, or interdigitated architecture.
decisions.final_value: Categorical characteristic identifying the arrangement and connectivity of flow channels in a flow field, such as parallel, serpentine, or interdigitated architecture.
decisions.rationale: The original labels an architecture category as quantitative.
decisions.implementation: Keep channel width, depth, number and hydraulic dimensions as separate characteristics.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents free msa weight percent based on qd for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Percentage mass ratio of unbound MSA ligand to quantum-dot material, calculated as 100 times the mass of free ligand divided by the stated quantum-dot reference mass.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents free msa weight percent based on qd for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: This is a free-ligand-to-quantum-dot mass ratio, rather than a mass fraction of the final mixture.
decisions.implementation: Before implementation, identify the chemical species abbreviated MSA and specify whether quantum-dot reference mass includes bound ligands. Do not infer the chemical expansion from the acronym alone.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents gas hourly space velocity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Volumetric gas feed rate at specified reference temperature and pressure divided by the mass of catalyst used in the reactor.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents gas hourly space velocity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The contextual L gcat⁻¹ h⁻¹ identifies catalyst-mass normalization, whereas conventional GHSV often uses catalyst-bed volume.
decisions.implementation: For the existing mass-normalized data, preferably rename the label to “mass-normalized gas volumetric feed rate”. Reserve gas hourly space velocity for volumetric gas feed rate divided by catalyst-bed volume, usually h⁻¹; do not silently reinterpret existing numbers.

decisions.current_value: A temporal characteristic that represents gel point time for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Elapsed time from the start of the specified curing protocol to the operational gelation criterion; for the stated rheological protocol, the criterion is the crossover at which storage modulus G′ equals loss modulus G″ at the selected oscillation frequency.
decisions.final_value: Elapsed time from the start of the specified curing protocol to the operational gelation criterion; for the stated rheological protocol, the criterion is the crossover at which storage modulus G′ equals loss modulus G″ at the selected oscillation frequency.
decisions.rationale: The crossover is a protocol-dependent operational criterion and is not universally the true critical gel point.  References 55.
decisions.implementation: Record frequency, strain amplitude, temperature, illumination protocol and time-zero event. Do not generalize the G′ = G″ criterion to all gelation measurements.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting characteristic grain/crystallite size estimated from XRD using Scherrer formula (reported ~5 nm for β-SiC at 1600°C).
decisions.recommended_value: Characteristic dimension of a microstructural grain, determined using a stated grain-size metric and characterization method.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting characteristic grain/crystallite size estimated from XRD using Scherrer formula (reported ~5 nm for β-SiC at 1600°C).
decisions.rationale: A physical grain dimension is not generally identical to a coherent crystallite-domain size inferred from X-ray diffraction.  References 47.
decisions.implementation: Use this definition only if retaining the GrainSize identity. The existing Scherrer-derived records should instead be assigned to a crystallite-domain-size class, whose definition is supplied as an alternative.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting percent contribution of graphitic/aliphatic carbon component in C 1s XPS deconvolution.
decisions.recommended_value: Percentage of the integrated C 1s X-ray photoelectron signal assigned to the graphitic sp²-carbon component under a stated peak-fitting model.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting percent contribution of graphitic/aliphatic carbon component in C 1s XPS deconvolution.
decisions.rationale: Graphitic carbon and a combined graphitic/aliphatic C–C/C–H component are not the same observable.
decisions.implementation: Use the proposed definition only when graphitic carbon is resolved. For the combined component currently described, rename the class to describe the combined C–C/C–H signal fraction and use the alternative. Do not equate XPS peak-area percentage with bulk carbon mass fraction.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting authors report anode 'ECSA' in units of mA·V·cm^-2 from H2 desorption peak integration; likely proportional to charge density (needs curation).
decisions.recommended_value: Potential integral of the baseline-corrected current density assigned to oxidative desorption of adsorbed hydrogen over a specified voltammetric peak, calculated as the integral of j(E) with respect to electrode potential E.
decisions.final_value: Potential integral of the baseline-corrected current density assigned to oxidative desorption of adsorbed hydrogen over a specified voltammetric peak, calculated as the integral of j(E) with respect to electrode potential E.
decisions.rationale: The integral has current-density times potential units; it is neither charge density nor electrochemically active area by itself.
decisions.implementation: For constant scan rate v, divide this potential integral by v to obtain hydrogen charge per the current-density reference area. Obtaining active Pt area requires an additional reference monolayer charge per Pt area. State the electrode-area basis and integration bounds. If the process is adsorbed-hydrogen oxidation, prefer a label without H₂, which can suggest molecular hydrogen evolution or desorption.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting half wave potential shift relative to nafion and determined in Accelerated Stress Test Voltage Cycling.
decisions.recommended_value: Difference between the oxygen-reduction half-wave potential of the investigated electrode and that of a matched electrode using Nafion ionomer, calculated as E₁/₂,test minus E₁/₂,Nafion.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting half wave potential shift relative to nafion and determined in Accelerated Stress Test Voltage Cycling.
decisions.rationale: The comparison needs a reference electrode formulation and sign convention; it is not inherently an accelerated-stress-test result.
decisions.implementation: Use the stated positive-for-test-higher convention only if consistent with source values; otherwise preserve the source convention explicitly. Match potential scale, electrolyte, loading and hydrodynamic conditions.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents henrys coefficient for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Henry solubility coefficient on an amount-concentration/partial-pressure basis, defined in the infinite-dilution limit as equilibrium dissolved-gas amount concentration divided by gas partial pressure.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents henrys coefficient for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Henry coefficients have several reciprocal or differently normalized conventions.  References 23.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only if source units and equation identify c/p. If p/c is used, select the alternative; other conventions require their corresponding explicit definition. Record gas, solvent or ionomer, temperature and pressure range.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting ohmic/HFR concept in RQ (discussed conceptually).
decisions.recommended_value: Ohmic resistance estimated from the high-frequency real-axis intercept of an electrochemical impedance spectrum of the specified cell or electrode assembly.
decisions.final_value: Ohmic resistance estimated from the high-frequency real-axis intercept of an electrochemical impedance spectrum of the specified cell or electrode assembly.
decisions.rationale: The existing text is a research-question note rather than a resistance definition.
decisions.implementation: Specify whether the value is resistance in ohms or area-specific resistance in ohm area. Record intercept-estimation method; an arbitrary high-frequency real component need not equal the true intercept.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting hydration number lambda and determined in Membrane Swelling Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Average number of water molecules per specified ion-exchange site in an ionomer, calculated as the amount of water divided by the amount of ion-exchange sites.
decisions.final_value: Average number of water molecules per specified ion-exchange site in an ionomer, calculated as the amount of water divided by the amount of ion-exchange sites.
decisions.rationale: The observable is the water-to-site amount ratio rather than a swelling measurement itself.
decisions.implementation: For sulfonated ionomers, identify whether sites are counted as sulfonic-acid or sulfonate groups and state conditioning. The definition does not impose a particular measurement technique.

decisions.current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents hydrogen oxidation charge constant for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Reference electric charge per unit true platinum surface area for oxidation of an adsorbed hydrogen monolayer under a specified electrochemical protocol.
decisions.final_value: Reference electric charge per unit true platinum surface area for oxidation of an adsorbed hydrogen monolayer under a specified electrochemical protocol.
decisions.rationale: The source context describes a surface-specific reference charge, not a universal total charge.
decisions.implementation: Record the numerical reference value, Pt surface assumption, electrolyte and convention used for active-area conversion; do not impose a universal constant.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting hydrolysis rate through membrane during conversion of sulfonyl fluoride to sulfonic acid groups.
decisions.recommended_value: Rate of conversion of sulfonyl-fluoride groups in a membrane into sulfonic-acid or sulfonate groups, expressed as change in the specified extent of conversion per unit time.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting hydrolysis rate through membrane during conversion of sulfonyl fluoride to sulfonic acid groups.
decisions.rationale: Chemical conversion rate and motion of a reaction front have different dimensions and should not share one definition.
decisions.implementation: Use the proposed definition when the source reports conversion/time. If it reports penetration distance/time, rename the characteristic to hydrolysis-front propagation speed and use the alternative. Specify whether acid or salt form is measured.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents hydrolysis rate slowdown factor for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of the hydrolysis rate at 75 °C to the hydrolysis rate at 25 °C for the same conversion observable and otherwise matched conditions.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents hydrolysis rate slowdown factor for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The original omits the orientation of the rate ratio.
decisions.implementation: Confirm the source defines slowdown as the high-temperature rate divided by the low-temperature rate; invert the definition if its reported factor uses the reciprocal. Specify whether the rates are conversion rates, fitted constants, or front speeds.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting impedance modulus slope K and determined in Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Potentiostatic.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting impedance modulus slope K and determined in Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Potentiostatic.
decisions.rationale: The physical slope cannot be identified without the independent variable and transformation of the impedance-modulus plot.
decisions.implementation: Retrieve the source figure or equation defining K. Identify whether it is d|Z|/df, dlog|Z|/dlogf, slope versus another frequency function, or a fitted circuit coefficient; record frequency interval, sign, log convention and units. Do not define K as a generic electrical resistance.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting initial catalytic activity loss percent and determined in Review Statement Extraction.
decisions.recommended_value: Percentage decrease in a specified catalytic activity from an identified initial reference state to an identified comparison state, calculated as 100 times the initial activity minus the comparison activity, divided by the initial activity.
decisions.final_value: Percentage decrease in a specified catalytic activity from an identified initial reference state to an identified comparison state, calculated as 100 times the initial activity minus the comparison activity, divided by the initial activity.
decisions.rationale: A percentage loss requires a baseline and sign convention; review-statement extraction is not the physical observable.
decisions.implementation: State the catalytic activity measure, initial state, comparison state and matched measurement conditions. A negative value denotes an activity gain under this convention.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents initial membrane water content lambda for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Initial membrane hydration number before the specified operation, equal to the amount of membrane water divided by the amount of membrane ion-exchange sites.
decisions.final_value: Initial membrane hydration number before the specified operation, equal to the amount of membrane water divided by the amount of membrane ion-exchange sites.
decisions.rationale: Lambda denotes water molecules per ionic site, not an unspecified water-content measure.
decisions.implementation: State the initial event, ionic-site identity and conditioning; for cold start, identify whether initial content excludes surface or channel water.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ink dilution ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of final diluted-ink suspension volume to the initial ink aliquot volume used for dilution.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents ink dilution ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Dilution ratio may mean final/initial volume or added-diluent/initial volume; those differ by one when volumes are additive.
decisions.implementation: Use only after confirming final/initial convention. Otherwise use the alternative. Record added volumes and avoid assuming strict volume additivity when precision requires it.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents inkjet printing spatial resolution for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Minimum feature dimension or separation that an inkjet-printing process can reproducibly distinguish in a printed pattern under specified printing and substrate conditions.
decisions.final_value: Minimum feature dimension or separation that an inkjet-printing process can reproducibly distinguish in a printed pattern under specified printing and substrate conditions.
decisions.rationale: Feature resolution and positional placement accuracy are different observables.
decisions.implementation: State the feature metric and reproducibility criterion. If existing source data describe droplet placement error, assign them to a separate placement-accuracy characteristic.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting ink storage stability duration and determined in Review Statement Extraction.
decisions.recommended_value: Elapsed storage time for which an ink satisfies a specified stability criterion under stated storage conditions.
decisions.final_value: Elapsed storage time for which an ink satisfies a specified stability criterion under stated storage conditions.
decisions.rationale: A stability duration requires an explicit criterion rather than an extraction activity.
decisions.implementation: Record the failure or censoring criterion, such as phase-separation threshold, particle-size change, or rheological change. Distinguish “stable for at least t” from a measured failure time.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting interfacial resistance.
decisions.recommended_value: Oxygen mass-transfer resistance associated with crossing a specified gas–ionomer interface, defined as the oxygen concentration drop across that interface divided by the oxygen molar flux on a stated reference-area basis.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting interfacial resistance.
decisions.rationale: The source aliases indicate gas-dissolution transport, while the existing name and definition could also mean electrical interfacial resistance.
decisions.implementation: Use this definition only after confirming the source convention and rename to “gas–ionomer interfacial oxygen transport resistance”; use TransportCharacteristic or SurfaceCharacteristic as parent then. If the source describes electrical resistance, use the alternative and retain ElectrochemicalCharacteristic.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents intrinsic viscosity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Dimensionless dilute-suspension viscosity coefficient equal to the limit of (ηᵣ − 1)/φ as particle volume fraction φ approaches zero, where ηᵣ is suspension viscosity divided by continuous-phase viscosity.
decisions.final_value: Dimensionless dilute-suspension viscosity coefficient equal to the limit of (ηᵣ − 1)/φ as particle volume fraction φ approaches zero, where ηᵣ is suspension viscosity divided by continuous-phase viscosity.
decisions.rationale: The contextual Krieger–Dougherty parameter is a volume-fraction-based dimensionless coefficient, unlike polymer-solution intrinsic viscosity expressed per mass concentration.
decisions.implementation: Prefer the label “suspension intrinsic-viscosity coefficient”. State the shear regime and the fitted Krieger–Dougherty equation; do not reuse polymer intrinsic-viscosity units.

decisions.current_value: A performance characteristic that represents ion exchange capacity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Amount of exchangeable ionic charge in an ion-exchange material divided by its dry mass, expressed as charge equivalents per unit mass.
decisions.final_value: Amount of exchangeable ionic charge in an ion-exchange material divided by its dry mass, expressed as charge equivalents per unit mass.
decisions.rationale: The definition needs the charge-equivalent numerator and dry-material basis.
decisions.implementation: State acid/salt form, drying method, measurement method and whether measured or theoretical IEC is reported. One milliequivalent per gram equals one millimole of monovalent exchangeable charge per gram.

decisions.current_value: A mechanical characteristic that represents ionic strength for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: One half of the sum, over all dissolved ionic species, of each species' amount concentration multiplied by the square of its charge number.
decisions.final_value: One half of the sum, over all dissolved ionic species, of each species' amount concentration multiplied by the square of its charge number.
decisions.rationale: All dissolved ions contribute; ionic strength is not generally equal to hydrogen-ion concentration.  References 16.
decisions.implementation: This definition adopts amount concentration. If a molality basis is required, create or clearly distinguish Iₘ = ½ Σᵢ mᵢ zᵢ². Do not treat a salt-free formulation as ion-free when acid or ionomer counterions are present.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting ionomer connected electrochemically active surface area and determined in Carbon Monoxide Stripping Voltammetry.
decisions.recommended_value: Electrochemically active platinum surface area supplied with protons through connected ionomer pathways under a protocol designed to distinguish that contribution from sites supplied through liquid-water pathways.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting ionomer connected electrochemically active surface area and determined in Carbon Monoxide Stripping Voltammetry.
decisions.rationale: Ordinary CO stripping alone does not prove selective measurement of ionomer-connected Pt area.
decisions.implementation: State the selective protocol, humidity and liquid-water conditions, Pt reference charge and normalization. If the source measures total accessible ECSA without selectivity, assign it to total ECSA instead.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents ionomer equivalent weight for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Dry ionomer mass per equivalent of exchangeable ionic charge.
decisions.final_value: Dry ionomer mass per equivalent of exchangeable ionic charge.
decisions.rationale: Equivalent weight requires a mass-per-charge-equivalent identity.
decisions.implementation: State the ionomer form and ionic-site type. For monovalent sites, one equivalent corresponds to one mole of sites; record the usual g eq⁻¹ basis.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ionomer mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of ionomer divided by the total mass of the explicitly specified mixture or material reference domain.
decisions.final_value: Mass of ionomer divided by the total mass of the explicitly specified mixture or material reference domain.
decisions.rationale: A mass fraction is a constituent/total ratio, not an ionomer-to-catalyst ratio.  References 15.
decisions.implementation: Record whether the reference domain is dry catalyst-layer solids, all ink constituents, or another declared domain. Do not impose a dry-solids basis on ink-mixture data; remove ratio aliases that imply a different denominator.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ionomer to catalyst mass ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of dry ionomer mass to the mass of the explicitly identified catalyst material in the same formulation or electrode.
decisions.final_value: Ratio of dry ionomer mass to the mass of the explicitly identified catalyst material in the same formulation or electrode.
decisions.rationale: Catalyst may mean supported catalyst or active metal; these denominators are not interchangeable.
decisions.implementation: Declare whether the catalyst denominator includes support and any binder. Use separate specializations or normalization metadata for supported-catalyst and metal-only ratios.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents ionomer uniformity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Quantitative measure of spatial uniformity of ionomer distribution over a defined material region, determined using a specified observable, sampling scale and mathematical statistic.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents ionomer uniformity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: No single conventional numerical uniformity index is implied by the current class name.
decisions.implementation: Before using existing numbers, identify the actual statistic, field being sampled and spatial region. If the source only states “uniform ionomer distribution”, represent that assertion as a qualitative descriptor instead of inventing a numerical score.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ircompensation fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Fraction of the estimated uncompensated ohmic voltage drop iR that is corrected by an electrochemical instrument or by post-processing.
decisions.final_value: Fraction of the estimated uncompensated ohmic voltage drop iR that is corrected by an electrochemical instrument or by post-processing.
decisions.rationale: The corrected quantity is an ohmic potential drop, not a composition fraction.
decisions.implementation: State the resistance-estimation method, correction procedure and whether the fraction is expressed on a 0–1 or 0–100 percent scale.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting kinetic current normalized to Geometric Area and determined in Rotating Ring Disk Voltammetry and Linear Sweep Voltammetry.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass-transport-corrected faradaic current representing the electrode reaction rate at a specified potential under the stated kinetic-current model.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting kinetic current normalized to Geometric Area and determined in Rotating Ring Disk Voltammetry and Linear Sweep Voltammetry.
decisions.rationale: Current divided by geometric electrode area is kinetic current density, not current.
decisions.implementation: To preserve the geometric-area-normalized source data, rename the existing class to KineticCurrentDensity and use the alternative. Otherwise retain KineticCurrent for amperes and migrate area-normalized records.

decisions.current_value: A count characteristic that represents knudsen number for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The dimensionless ratio of molecular mean free path to the stated characteristic transport length, such as a pore diameter.
decisions.final_value: The dimensionless ratio of molecular mean free path to the stated characteristic transport length, such as a pore diameter.
decisions.rationale: The quantity is a ratio of lengths rather than a count.
decisions.implementation: State the gas, temperature, pressure and characteristic-length convention; pore diameter and radius give different numeric Knudsen numbers.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting large pore fraction above 150 nm and determined in FIBSEM Tomography Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Fraction of a specified pore population having a stated pore-size metric greater than 150 nm, calculated using an explicitly declared count, area or pore-volume weighting.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting large pore fraction above 150 nm and determined in FIBSEM Tomography Measurement.
decisions.rationale: The threshold alone does not determine the fraction’s denominator or weighting.
decisions.implementation: Record the pore-size metric, segmentation method, analyzed region and weighting. Do not compare count fractions directly with pore-volume fractions.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents laser pulse length for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Temporal duration of a laser pulse, measured using a stated criterion on its time-dependent intensity profile.
decisions.final_value: Temporal duration of a laser pulse, measured using a stated criterion on its time-dependent intensity profile.
decisions.rationale: The source describes nanosecond duration, rather than spatial pulse length.
decisions.implementation: Prefer label “laser pulse duration”; specify full width at half maximum, 1/e width, or the source’s duration convention.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting lattice distortion percent.
decisions.recommended_value: Percentage change in a specified lattice parameter relative to a declared reference, calculated as 100 times the measured parameter minus the reference parameter, divided by the reference parameter.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting lattice distortion percent.
decisions.rationale: A lattice-parameter change and a distribution-based microstrain metric are distinct quantities.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only if the source reports a relative lattice-parameter change. If it reports root-mean-square microstrain or another distortion invariant, retrieve its equation and use that specific identity. State signed versus absolute convention.
