decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents li cl to bi molar ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Amount ratio of lithium chloride to benzimidazole repeat units in the specified solution or formulation.
decisions.final_value: Amount ratio of lithium chloride to benzimidazole repeat units in the specified solution or formulation.
decisions.rationale: The description identifies BI as benzimidazole units, not elemental bismuth.
decisions.implementation: Write the ratio as n(LiCl)/n(benzimidazole repeat units); identify the polymer and counting convention for its benzimidazole units.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting local gas transport resistance normalized to Geometric Area and determined in Oxygen Gain/Loss Measurement and Limiting Current Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Contribution to gas mass-transfer resistance assigned to a specified local catalyst region or interface, defined using a declared gas concentration or partial-pressure driving force divided by molar flux on a stated area basis.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting local gas transport resistance normalized to Geometric Area and determined in Oxygen Gain/Loss Measurement and Limiting Current Measurement.
decisions.rationale: A local resistance requires both a physical region and a driving-force/flux convention.
decisions.implementation: Identify the transported gas, region and separation method. Keep concentration-normalized and pressure-normalized resistance distinct, and record geometric or catalyst-area normalization.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting local oxygen transport resistance normalized to Geometric Area and determined in Oxygen Gain/Loss Measurement, O2–N2 Switching Measurement, and Through-Plane Gas Transport Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Oxygen mass-transfer resistance associated with the immediate environment of catalyst reaction sites, determined using a stated oxygen driving-force and flux convention and a declared reference area.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting local oxygen transport resistance normalized to Geometric Area and determined in Oxygen Gain/Loss Measurement, O2–N2 Switching Measurement, and Through-Plane Gas Transport Measurement.
decisions.rationale: Local catalyst-region resistance is not automatically identical to the entire pressure-independent resistance.
decisions.implementation: State whether the value is normalized to geometric area or Pt area, how local resistance is separated, and which ionomer-film or interfacial contributions are included. Do not equate it with all Knudsen or pressure-independent contributions.

decisions.current_value: A statistical characteristic that represents log normal standard deviation for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Standard deviation of the natural logarithm of particle diameter divided by a fixed reference diameter, for a lognormally distributed diameter variable.
decisions.final_value: A statistical characteristic that represents log normal standard deviation for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The standard deviation of log diameter differs from geometric standard deviation and ordinary diameter standard deviation.
decisions.implementation: Adopt after checking the source uses natural-log width σ; geometric standard deviation is exp(σ). If the paper uses log base 10 or reports geometric standard deviation, state that convention instead.

decisions.current_value: A mechanical characteristic that represents magnetic field strength for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Magnitude of the magnetic field strength H at the specified location, expressed in amperes per metre.
decisions.final_value: A mechanical characteristic that represents magnetic field strength for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: H and magnetic flux density B are distinct quantities despite frequently sharing the informal name magnetic field.
decisions.implementation: If existing source values are in tesla, rename the characteristic to magnetic flux density and use the alternative; do not change numeric units without the appropriate relation and medium information.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents manufacturing throughput increase factor for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Ratio of manufacturing throughput for the investigated process to throughput for a declared reference process, calculated using the same output measure and time basis.
decisions.final_value: Ratio of manufacturing throughput for the investigated process to throughput for a declared reference process, calculated using the same output measure and time basis.
decisions.rationale: A throughput ratio differs from a fractional or percentage increase.
decisions.implementation: Specify output metric, such as coated area or accepted product count per time, and the reference process. Under this convention a factor of two means twice the baseline throughput.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting mass activity and determined in MEAPolarization, Rotating Ring Disk Voltammetry, and Linear Sweep Voltammetry.
decisions.recommended_value: Electrochemical reaction current divided by the mass of the explicitly specified catalyst or active-metal reference material, measured at a stated potential and conditions.
decisions.final_value: Electrochemical reaction current divided by the mass of the explicitly specified catalyst or active-metal reference material, measured at a stated potential and conditions.
decisions.rationale: The mass denominator is essential for comparison of catalytic performance.
decisions.implementation: Record Pt, PGM, total-metal, supported-catalyst or other denominator; state whether the numerator is kinetic or measured current and whether current magnitude is used.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting mass fractal dimension from low-q USAXS power-law scaling; higher indicates greater agglomeration.
decisions.recommended_value: The exponent relating aggregate mass to characteristic size through a power law over a specified scale range, estimated using a stated structural or scattering model.
decisions.final_value: The exponent relating aggregate mass to characteristic size through a power law over a specified scale range, estimated using a stated structural or scattering model.
decisions.rationale: A higher mass-fractal dimension indicates greater aggregate compactness within that model, rather than universally a larger degree of agglomeration.  References 24, 48.
decisions.implementation: For scattering-derived values, state the fitted q range and distinguish the mass-fractal regime from surface-fractal or Porod regimes.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting mass transport resistance increase due to local percent.
decisions.recommended_value: The percentage of a specified increase in total mass-transfer resistance attributable to the change in local resistance, equal to 100 times the local-resistance change divided by the total-resistance change.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting mass transport resistance increase due to local percent.
decisions.rationale: The source alias indicates a contribution share; that differs from percent growth of local resistance relative to its own baseline.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only if the source defines an attributable share. Identify both states and common resistance normalization; the ratio is undefined when ΔR_total is zero. Use the alternative for local-resistance relative increase.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting mass transport resistance increase percent.
decisions.recommended_value: The percentage increase in mass-transfer resistance relative to an identified reference state, equal to 100 times the difference between test and reference resistance divided by the reference resistance.
decisions.final_value: The percentage increase in mass-transfer resistance relative to an identified reference state, equal to 100 times the difference between test and reference resistance divided by the reference resistance.
decisions.rationale: The reference state and denominator were absent.
decisions.implementation: Use the same gas, driving-force convention, area basis and conditions for both resistances; identify the comparison states.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting maximum N2 adsorption volume (proxy for pore volume).
decisions.recommended_value: Maximum measured nitrogen uptake in a specified adsorption experiment, expressed as an equivalent gas volume at stated reference conditions per declared sample amount.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting maximum N2 adsorption volume (proxy for pore volume).
decisions.rationale: Gas-equivalent uptake and liquid-equivalent pore volume are different observables.
decisions.implementation: State measurement temperature, maximum relative pressure, gas reference temperature/pressure and sample normalization. If source data are condensed-liquid-equivalent pore volumes, define and label that quantity separately.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting max adsorption volume water.
decisions.recommended_value: Maximum measured water uptake in a specified adsorption experiment, expressed as an equivalent liquid-water volume per declared sample amount at stated conditions.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting max adsorption volume water.
decisions.rationale: The existing term does not identify whether the quoted volume is liquid equivalent or vapour equivalent.
decisions.implementation: Use only after confirming liquid-equivalent convention and conversion density. Record temperature and maximum water activity; if the source uses vapour-equivalent volume, use the alternative.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents maximum particle volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The maximum-packing particle volume-fraction parameter in a specified suspension-viscosity model, representing the model's limiting packing fraction at which the predicted viscosity diverges.
decisions.final_value: The maximum-packing particle volume-fraction parameter in a specified suspension-viscosity model, representing the model's limiting packing fraction at which the predicted viscosity diverges.
decisions.rationale: The contextual parameter is a fitted limiting-packing parameter rather than an unspecified geometric maximum.
decisions.implementation: State the Krieger–Dougherty equation, fitting shear regime and phase-volume basis; distinguish model extrapolation from directly measured maximum packing.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting mean flow pore diameter and determined in Mercury Intrusion Porosimetry Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Equivalent through-pore diameter calculated from the capillary-flow pressure at which the wetted-sample gas-flow curve intersects one half of the dry-sample gas-flow curve.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting mean flow pore diameter and determined in Mercury Intrusion Porosimetry Measurement.
decisions.rationale: Mean-flow pore size is an operational capillary-flow-porometry quantity, not simply a mercury-intrusion mean diameter.  References 32.
decisions.implementation: Replace the stated measurement association with capillary flow porometry if source evidence supports it. If the original method really was mercury intrusion, preserve the source data under a separately defined intrusion-distribution pore-diameter metric. State wetting liquid, contact angle and pore model.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting pore volume attributed to mesopores (>2 nm in cited convention); reported/compared in cm^3/g.
decisions.recommended_value: Volume of pores with widths approximately 2–50 nm, per unit sample mass when reported as specific pore volume, determined using a stated pore-size analysis method.
decisions.final_value: Volume of pores with widths approximately 2–50 nm, per unit sample mass when reported as specific pore volume, determined using a stated pore-size analysis method.
decisions.rationale: A lower threshold of 2 nm alone includes macropores as well as mesopores.  References 19.
decisions.implementation: Keep the method and mass basis explicit. If the source truly reports all pores wider than 2 nm, retain that value under a separate “pore volume above 2 nm” characteristic rather than relabeling it mesopore volume.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting upper bound of reported µm-scale pore size tunability range (10–20 µm).
decisions.recommended_value: Upper bound of the micrometre-scale pore-size range in the specified material, determined using a stated pore-size metric and characterization method.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting upper bound of reported µm-scale pore size tunability range (10–20 µm).
decisions.rationale: The recorded 10–20 µm range concerns macropores, not micropores in adsorption terminology.  References 20.
decisions.implementation: To preserve the represented data, rename the class to MicrometreScalePoreSizeMax or an appropriate macropore-range-upper-bound label. Do not change the numbers to nanometres. If retaining the MicroporeSizeMax identity, move the existing data and use a definition restricted to pores not exceeding approximately 2 nm.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting lower bound of reported µm-scale pore size tunability range (10–20 µm).
decisions.recommended_value: Lower bound of the micrometre-scale pore-size range in the specified material, determined using a stated pore-size metric and characterization method.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting lower bound of reported µm-scale pore size tunability range (10–20 µm).
decisions.rationale: The recorded 10–20 µm range concerns macropores, not micropores in adsorption terminology.  References 20.
decisions.implementation: To preserve the represented data, rename the class to MicrometreScalePoreSizeMin or an appropriate macropore-range-lower-bound label. Do not change the numbers to nanometres. If retaining the MicroporeSizeMin identity, move the existing data and use a definition restricted to pores not exceeding approximately 2 nm.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents msa mass for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of the ligand identified as MSA added to a specified ligand-exchange batch.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents msa mass for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The batch mass observable is recoverable, but the chemical expansion of MSA is not established by the supplied record.
decisions.implementation: Identify MSA by full chemical name and a chemical identifier before final implementation. If MSA is delivered as a solution, distinguish mass of ligand solute from mass of solution; do not infer mercaptosuccinic acid or another species solely from the acronym.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents msa weight percent of qd powder for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Percentage mass ratio of added MSA ligand to the initial quantum-dot powder, calculated as 100 times the ligand mass divided by the initial powder mass.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents msa weight percent of qd powder for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The recorded basis is initial quantum-dot powder mass, not total final formulation mass.
decisions.implementation: Expand MSA to a verified chemical name and identify whether the powder includes pre-existing ligands. Prefer “MSA-to-quantum-dot-powder mass ratio (%)” to avoid implying a final-mixture mass fraction.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents nafion fiber loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass of dry Nafion fibers deposited on a membrane divided by the geometric area of the coated membrane region.
decisions.final_value: Mass of dry Nafion fibers deposited on a membrane divided by the geometric area of the coated membrane region.
decisions.rationale: The source context identifies areal mass loading rather than a mass fraction.
decisions.implementation: State dry-mass determination, coated area and whether both membrane faces are included.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting atomic percent (at.%) ratio of nitrogen to carbon measured by EDX in CNT forests.
decisions.recommended_value: Nitrogen-to-carbon atomic ratio expressed as a percentage, calculated as 100 times the amount of nitrogen atoms divided by the amount of carbon atoms in the analyzed region.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting atomic percent (at.%) ratio of nitrogen to carbon measured by EDX in CNT forests.
decisions.rationale: An N/C ratio and nitrogen atomic percent among all elements have different denominators.
decisions.implementation: Use the proposed definition only if source “N/C (at.%)” means 100 n_N/n_C; rename to “nitrogen-to-carbon atomic ratio (%)”. If the source instead means nitrogen atomic percentage, use the alternative. Identify EDX quantification basis and elements included.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting non pt catalyst volumetric activity and determined in Review Statement Extraction.
decisions.recommended_value: Electrochemical reaction current generated by a non-platinum catalyst divided by the explicitly specified catalyst or catalyst-layer reference volume at stated potential and conditions.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting non pt catalyst volumetric activity and determined in Review Statement Extraction.
decisions.rationale: Volumetric activity needs both a reaction-rate numerator and a declared volume denominator.
decisions.implementation: Specify whether the denominator is catalyst-solid, catalyst-layer, or another volume and whether current is kinetic or measured. If source activity is a chemical reaction rate rather than current, define a separate rate-based specialization.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting other fatty acids mass fraction and determined in Gas Chromatography Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Combined mass of fatty acids outside an explicitly enumerated principal-fatty-acid set divided by the total fatty-acid mass in the analyzed sample.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting other fatty acids mass fraction and determined in Gas Chromatography Measurement.
decisions.rationale: The residual category requires both its excluded species and its mass denominator.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only if the analysis uses total fatty-acid mass. List the principal species excluded from “other”; if the source denominator is whole-sample mass, use the alternative. Do not assume chromatographic area percent equals mass percent without a justified response convention.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting oxirane content and determined in Epoxy Equivalent Titration Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass fraction of oxygen atoms present in oxirane rings in the specified material.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting oxirane content and determined in Epoxy Equivalent Titration Measurement.
decisions.rationale: Oxirane-oxygen mass fraction, epoxide equivalents per mass and epoxy equivalent weight are related but different quantities.
decisions.implementation: Use only if the source reports oxirane oxygen content. For a titration reported as epoxide equivalents per mass, use the alternative and a corresponding label. Record titration conversion and reporting basis; do not infer basis from the method name alone.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents oxygen solubility in ionomer for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Equilibrium amount concentration of molecular oxygen dissolved in a specified ionomer at stated temperature, oxygen partial pressure and ionomer hydration state.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents oxygen solubility in ionomer for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: An equilibrium dissolved concentration differs from a pressure-normalized solubility coefficient.  References 23.
decisions.implementation: Adopt when the source reports dissolved oxygen concentration. For c/p-type data, use a separately identified Henry solubility coefficient and the alternative. State dry, swollen or other volume basis.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents palladium chloride concentration ppm for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: Mass fraction of palladium chloride in the specified mixture expressed in parts per million, equal to one million times the mass of palladium chloride divided by total mixture mass.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents palladium chloride concentration ppm for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The reporting basis of ppm and whether it refers to compound mass or elemental palladium must be distinguished.
decisions.implementation: Use only if the source reports mass-based PdCl₂ ppm; verify hydrate or anhydrous form. For Pd-equivalent mass concentration, relabel and use the alternative. A stated mg L⁻¹ value is not automatically ppm without an explicit density or convention.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting 10th percentile of particle size distribution from DLS (D10).
decisions.recommended_value: Particle diameter at the 10th percentile of a specified cumulative particle-size distribution, such that 10% of the declared distribution weighting lies at or below that diameter.
decisions.final_value: Particle diameter at the 10th percentile of a specified cumulative particle-size distribution, such that 10% of the declared distribution weighting lies at or below that diameter.
decisions.rationale: The numerical percentile is meaningful only with its distribution weighting and particle-size metric.  References 49.
decisions.implementation: For DLS, specify hydrodynamic diameter, intensity/volume/number weighting and inversion or conversion method. The class can remain generic if every value carries that basis explicitly; do not infer volume weighting from an alias alone.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting 50th percentile (median) of particle size distribution from DLS (D50).
decisions.recommended_value: Particle diameter at the 50th percentile of a specified cumulative particle-size distribution, such that 50% of the declared distribution weighting lies at or below that diameter.
decisions.final_value: Particle diameter at the 50th percentile of a specified cumulative particle-size distribution, such that 50% of the declared distribution weighting lies at or below that diameter.
decisions.rationale: The numerical percentile is meaningful only with its distribution weighting and particle-size metric.  References 49.
decisions.implementation: For DLS, specify hydrodynamic diameter, intensity/volume/number weighting and inversion or conversion method. The class can remain generic if every value carries that basis explicitly; do not infer volume weighting from an alias alone.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting 90th percentile of particle size distribution from DLS (D90).
decisions.recommended_value: Particle diameter at the 90th percentile of a specified cumulative particle-size distribution, such that 90% of the declared distribution weighting lies at or below that diameter.
decisions.final_value: Particle diameter at the 90th percentile of a specified cumulative particle-size distribution, such that 90% of the declared distribution weighting lies at or below that diameter.
decisions.rationale: The numerical percentile is meaningful only with its distribution weighting and particle-size metric.  References 49.
decisions.implementation: For DLS, specify hydrodynamic diameter, intensity/volume/number weighting and inversion or conversion method. The class can remain generic if every value carries that basis explicitly; do not infer volume weighting from an alias alone.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting maximum (peak) power density extracted from polarization curve.
decisions.recommended_value: Maximum electrical output power per declared electrode-area, system-volume or mass reference, obtained over a specified operating curve under stated conditions.
decisions.final_value: Maximum electrical output power per declared electrode-area, system-volume or mass reference, obtained over a specified operating curve under stated conditions.
decisions.rationale: A peak power density requires a declared normalization basis; electrode area, volume and mass are not interchangeable.
decisions.implementation: Record the reference quantity and units for every value. Prefer an area-specific subclass for W cm⁻², a volumetric subclass for W cm⁻³, and a mass-specific subclass for W g⁻¹; do not impose area normalization on existing records without evidence.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting peroxide yield and determined in Rotating Ring Disk Voltammetry.
decisions.recommended_value: The fraction of molecular oxygen consumed in an oxygen-reduction reaction that forms hydrogen peroxide or hydroperoxide, expressed as a fraction or percentage and inferred from rotating ring-disk electrode currents using the calibrated ring collection efficiency.
decisions.final_value: The fraction of molecular oxygen consumed in an oxygen-reduction reaction that forms hydrogen peroxide or hydroperoxide, expressed as a fraction or percentage and inferred from rotating ring-disk electrode currents using the calibrated ring collection efficiency.
decisions.rationale: Identifies molecular product selectivity rather than electron-based Faradaic efficiency.
decisions.implementation: For a disk producing only the two- and four-electron ORR products and a ring that quantitatively oxidizes peroxide, peroxide percent = 200(|I_ring|/N)/(|I_disk| + |I_ring|/N), using corrected currents and collection efficiency N. Record electrolyte, potentials and correction protocol; do not equate this molecular fraction with peroxide Faradaic efficiency.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents pgm on support weight percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The mass of platinum-group metals in a supported catalyst divided by the total dry mass of those metals and their support, multiplied by 100.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents pgm on support weight percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Conventional supported-catalyst weight percent requires the total-catalyst denominator.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only after confirming the source reports metal weight percent of the supported catalyst. If it reports metal/support mass ratio, use the alternative and rename accordingly.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents phosphoric acid loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The mass of phosphoric acid added to a cathode catalyst layer divided by the geometric electrode area to which the acid is applied.
decisions.final_value: The mass of phosphoric acid added to a cathode catalyst layer divided by the geometric electrode area to which the acid is applied.
decisions.rationale: The supplied context explicitly identifies areal loading, which differs from a molar acid-doping ratio.
decisions.implementation: Label as phosphoric-acid areal loading; record whether the acid mass is calculated as neat H3PO4 or includes water in the acid solution.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents piston displacement a 1 for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The downward displacement of the dispensing piston during the extrusion stroke used to deliver ink for one printed pillar.
decisions.final_value: The downward displacement of the dispensing piston during the extrusion stroke used to deliver ink for one printed pillar.
decisions.rationale: Identifies the source-described extrusion stroke rather than an unspecified displacement.
decisions.implementation: Record displacement sign convention and whether the value is a stroke magnitude or a signed coordinate difference.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents piston displacement a 2 for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The upward retraction displacement of the dispensing piston applied after pillar stretching to halt ink delivery.
decisions.final_value: The upward retraction displacement of the dispensing piston applied after pillar stretching to halt ink delivery.
decisions.rationale: Identifies the source-described retraction stroke rather than an unspecified displacement.
decisions.implementation: Record displacement sign convention and whether the value is a stroke magnitude or a signed coordinate difference.

decisions.current_value: Degree of molecular alignment induced in the adjacent ionomer film by the platinum surface.
decisions.final_value: Degree of molecular alignment induced in the adjacent ionomer film by the platinum surface.
decisions.rationale: The record does not identify the orientation observable or normalization represented by degree.
decisions.implementation: Retrieve the source equation: identify which ionomer vector/group is oriented, the direction relative to the Pt surface, and whether the value is an orientational order parameter, angular statistic, aligned fraction or fitted coefficient. These alternatives cannot share one numerical definition.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents polydispersity index for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: A dimensionless measure of the breadth of the distribution of decay rates obtained by cumulant analysis of a dynamic-light-scattering correlation function, equal to the second cumulant divided by the square of the mean decay rate.
decisions.final_value: DLSPolydispersityIndex | MolarMassDispersity
decisions.rationale: The description establishes DLS cumulant polydispersity; it is different from polymer molar-mass dispersity.  References 25.
decisions.implementation: Use preferred label DLS polydispersity index. Remove Mw/Mn as an alias; if needed, create a separate molar-mass dispersity class defined as mass-average molar mass divided by number-average molar mass.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents polymer force exponential coefficient for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents polymer force exponential coefficient for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The source-specific symbol does not establish the exponential force equation or the mathematical role of the coefficient.
decisions.implementation: Retrieve the DEM polymer-force law containing k2^(polymer), including the separation variable, sign convention, and units. Do not assume it is a decay constant or insert a guessed exponential equation.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents polymer force proportionality constant for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents polymer force proportionality constant for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The proportionality constant cannot be uniquely identified without the force law it multiplies.
decisions.implementation: Retrieve the DEM polymer-force equation containing k1^(polymer), identify the multiplied term and interacting entities, and derive the coefficient units from that equation.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents polymer interaction distance for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents polymer interaction distance for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: A length scale in an interaction model could denote center separation, surface gap, range, cutoff or decay length.
decisions.implementation: Retrieve the force or energy equation containing L^(polymer) and identify exactly which geometric distance it represents. Specify whether it is an input range parameter or a measured separation.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting acid dissociation constant (pKa) of polymer functional group (dimensionless).
decisions.recommended_value: The negative base-10 logarithm of the acid dissociation constant of a specified ionizable group in a polymer, for a stated medium, temperature and equilibrium convention.
decisions.final_value: The negative base-10 logarithm of the acid dissociation constant of a specified ionizable group in a polymer, for a stated medium, temperature and equilibrium convention.
decisions.rationale: pKa is -log10(Ka), not Ka itself.  References 13.
decisions.implementation: Record apparent versus thermodynamic pKa where relevant to a polyelectrolyte; do not equate measurements at different ionic strengths or protonation states without qualification.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents poss content relative to ionomer for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The mass of polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane additive divided by the mass of ionomer in the specified catalyst-layer formulation, multiplied by 100 when expressed as a percentage.
decisions.final_value: The mass of polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane additive divided by the mass of ionomer in the specified catalyst-layer formulation, multiplied by 100 when expressed as a percentage.
decisions.rationale: The source context fixes a mass-of-additive to mass-of-ionomer basis.
decisions.implementation: Specify the POSS chemistry and dry ionomer mass. This percentage can exceed 100 and is not the POSS mass fraction of the entire layer.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting power efficiency for LED device (lm/W).
decisions.recommended_value: The luminous flux emitted by an LED device divided by its electrical input power under specified operating conditions.
decisions.final_value: LEDLuminousEfficacy
decisions.rationale: The supplied lm/W observable is device luminous efficacy, rather than a power-conversion efficiency.  References 46.
decisions.implementation: Rename the preferred label to LED luminous efficacy and preferably mint a correspondingly named class IRI. If dimensionless power-conversion efficiency is also needed, define a separate class as optical radiant power divided by electrical input power.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting printability Z number and determined in Ink Printability Assessment.
decisions.recommended_value: The dimensionless inverse Ohnesorge number, equal to the square root of the product of liquid density, surface tension and stated characteristic jetting length divided by dynamic viscosity, used as an indicator of inkjet-fluid printability.
decisions.final_value: The dimensionless inverse Ohnesorge number, equal to the square root of the product of liquid density, surface tension and stated characteristic jetting length divided by dynamic viscosity, used as an indicator of inkjet-fluid printability.
decisions.rationale: Identifies the defining physical ratio rather than repeating the metric name.  References 28.
decisions.implementation: Specify whether L is nozzle diameter, nozzle radius or another length. Do not encode a universal printable Z interval; experimental ranges depend on the printing system.

decisions.current_value: A morphology coefficient used in a parameterized probability-density representation of material structure.
decisions.final_value: A morphology coefficient used in a parameterized probability-density representation of material structure.
decisions.rationale: The symbol k is not linked to an identified probability-density function.
decisions.implementation: Supply the complete probability-density equation, the structural random variable and its support, and whether k is a shape, scale, exponent or normalization parameter. No replacement equation can be recovered from the record alone.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents propylene glycol methyl ether volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The volume of propylene glycol methyl ether used in the solvent mixture divided by the total solvent-volume basis specified for that mixture.
decisions.final_value: The volume of propylene glycol methyl ether used in the solvent mixture divided by the total solvent-volume basis specified for that mixture.
decisions.rationale: Identifies a constituent composition ratio and its denominator.
decisions.implementation: State whether the denominator is the sum of separately dispensed solvent volumes or the measured final mixture volume, and whether a value is a fraction or percentage. These conventions differ for non-additive liquid mixtures.

decisions.current_value: A layer thickness that represents proton conduct layer thickness fraction in mcl for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The through-plane thickness of the designated proton-conducting sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the cathode multilayer catalyst layer.
decisions.final_value: The through-plane thickness of the designated proton-conducting sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the cathode multilayer catalyst layer.
decisions.rationale: Defines the dimensionless geometric fraction described in the contextual record.
decisions.implementation: Identify the designated sublayer X and whether values are fractions or percentages; use the same reference state and spatial averaging convention for both thicknesses.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting pseudo double layer capacitance and determined in Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Potentiostatic.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting pseudo double layer capacitance and determined in Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Potentiostatic.
decisions.rationale: The supplied name does not distinguish a true effective capacitance, a pseudocapacitance, or the magnitude parameter of a constant-phase element.
decisions.implementation: Retrieve the equivalent circuit and fitted impedance/admittance equation. If the fitted element is a CPE, define Q in Y = Q(j omega)^alpha and keep alpha and any Q-to-effective-capacitance conversion separate. If a capacitance in farads is reported, identify its physical/effective meaning and conversion formula. Do not silently rename Q as capacitance.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting pt chemical surface area and determined in Electron Microscopy Imaging.
decisions.recommended_value: The physical surface area of platinum particles estimated from electron-microscopy measurements of their size, shape or reconstructed morphology.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting pt chemical surface area and determined in Electron Microscopy Imaging.
decisions.rationale: Microscopy estimates geometric Pt surface rather than directly establishing electrochemical accessibility.
decisions.implementation: Prefer label microscopy-derived Pt physical surface area. Confirm whether the source reports total area or area per Pt mass before adopting: the replacement is for total area; for m2/g_Pt use the alternative. Check overlap with PhysicalSurfaceAreaPtCatalyst before adding a duplicate.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ptfe loading fraction of solids for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The mass of polytetrafluoroethylene divided by the total dry-solid mass of the specified ink or layer formulation.
decisions.final_value: The mass of polytetrafluoroethylene divided by the total dry-solid mass of the specified ink or layer formulation.
decisions.rationale: The wt.% of solids context identifies a dry-solid mass basis.
decisions.implementation: Multiply by 100 for percentage. State which components are counted as dry solids and whether the PTFE is reported as dry polymer rather than dispersion mass.

decisions.current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents pt hydrogen adsorption specific charge for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The electrical charge associated with adsorption or desorption of hydrogen divided by the platinum surface area to which that charge is assigned, used as a calibration charge density for hydrogen-adsorption-based Pt surface-area determination.
decisions.final_value: The electrical charge associated with adsorption or desorption of hydrogen divided by the platinum surface area to which that charge is assigned, used as a calibration charge density for hydrogen-adsorption-based Pt surface-area determination.
decisions.rationale: Identifies the area-normalized calibration quantity, rather than charge per catalyst mass.
decisions.implementation: Record surface/electrolyte conditions, selected adsorption/desorption branch and background subtraction. A conventional calibration value is protocol-dependent; do not hard-code one universal value.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting phenomenon/metric describing reduced ORR activity due to adsorption/poisoning of Pt by ionomer sulfonate groups (review discussion).
decisions.recommended_value: An inhibited electrocatalytic state of a platinum surface caused by adsorption of ionomer-associated species under the specified reaction and environmental conditions.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting phenomenon/metric describing reduced ORR activity due to adsorption/poisoning of Pt by ionomer sulfonate groups (review discussion).
decisions.rationale: Separates the scientifically meaningful poisoning effect from an undefined numeric metric.
decisions.implementation: Adopt this qualitative property only if the class denotes the effect. If a measured numeric quantity is intended, define a separate activity-loss ratio or adsorbate coverage with its baseline and test conditions; if the class denotes adsorption as a process, reclassify it in the Process branch instead.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents pt ru on carbon weight percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The combined mass of platinum and ruthenium divided by the total dry mass of the PtRu/carbon supported catalyst, multiplied by 100.
decisions.final_value: The combined mass of platinum and ruthenium divided by the total dry mass of the PtRu/carbon supported catalyst, multiplied by 100.
decisions.rationale: The context identifies total metal content of the bimetallic catalyst.
decisions.implementation: Keep the Pt/Ru atomic or mass ratio in a separate characteristic. If a source instead reports Pt-only content, map it to a separately defined Pt mass fraction.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting relative increase in mean current density per Pt surface (structure 1 reported 22% higher than structure 2).
decisions.recommended_value: The difference between platinum-surface-area-specific current in a test structure and in a reference structure, divided by the platinum-surface-area-specific current in the reference structure under matched conditions.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting relative increase in mean current density per Pt surface (structure 1 reported 22% higher than structure 2).
decisions.rationale: The supplied observable is a relative change in area-specific current, not an accessible-Pt-area utilization fraction.
decisions.implementation: Rename to relative increase in Pt-area-specific current. Multiply by 100 if expressed as percent; identify the potential and both structures. If Pt utilization is truly intended, use a separately defined accessible-Pt-area/physical-Pt-area metric.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting description=Average power density delivered during a galvanostatic discharge pulse (energy/time over pulse).
decisions.recommended_value: The average electrical power delivered during a specified discharge pulse divided by an explicitly stated normalization area, volume or mass, with average pulse power equal to the energy delivered during the pulse divided by its duration.
decisions.final_value: The average electrical power delivered during a specified discharge pulse divided by an explicitly stated normalization area, volume or mass, with average pulse power equal to the energy delivered during the pulse divided by its duration.
decisions.rationale: Restores the missing normalization required for any power-density quantity without guessing its basis.
decisions.implementation: This is a family definition, not permission to mix bases. Create/select a subclass for areal, volumetric or mass-specific pulse power and identify the denominator entity in every data record. If a single basis was intended by the source, narrow this class to that basis.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting quantum dot loading weight percent.
decisions.recommended_value: The mass of quantum dots divided by the total dry mass of the composite containing them, multiplied by 100.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting quantum dot loading weight percent.
decisions.rationale: A weight percentage needs an explicit material denominator.
decisions.implementation: Use only if the source reports weight percent of the dry composite. If the reported denominator is host alone or wet ink, use the corresponding alternative and a label that states that basis.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents ramp rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The rate of change of the heat-treatment temperature with elapsed time during a specified temperature-program segment.
decisions.final_value: The rate of change of the heat-treatment temperature with elapsed time during a specified temperature-program segment.
decisions.rationale: The description fixes this otherwise ambiguous ramp rate as thermal.
decisions.implementation: Prefer label temperature ramp rate; state signed dT/dt or positive heating/cooling magnitude and use the sample or programmed temperature consistently.

decisions.current_value: A layer thickness that represents reaction layer thickness fraction in mcl for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The through-plane thickness of the designated reaction sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the cathode multilayer catalyst layer.
decisions.final_value: The through-plane thickness of the designated reaction sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the cathode multilayer catalyst layer.
decisions.rationale: Defines a geometric fraction rather than a thickness.
decisions.implementation: Identify sublayer Y and fraction/percent convention; use the same reference state and averaging convention for numerator and denominator.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting temperature at which reduction of a specific oxide (or binder removal step) initiates under given atmosphere and heating rate.
decisions.recommended_value: The temperature at which reduction of a specified reducible species first satisfies the stated detection criterion during a defined atmosphere and heating protocol.
decisions.final_value: The temperature at which reduction of a specified reducible species first satisfies the stated detection criterion during a defined atmosphere and heating protocol.
decisions.rationale: Binder removal is not necessarily a reduction reaction.
decisions.implementation: Define the onset criterion, reducing-gas composition and heating rate; move non-reductive binder removal to a separate characteristic.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents reference concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The concentration assigned to an identified chemical species in a specified phase at the reference state of a defined kinetic or transport model.
decisions.final_value: The concentration assigned to an identified chemical species in a specified phase at the reference state of a defined kinetic or transport model.
decisions.rationale: Clarifies the role of a reference concentration without inventing the model species or reference state.
decisions.implementation: For the PEMFC CFD application, record the species, phase, concentration basis, reference temperature/pressure and the equation in which this value is used. Distinct physical reference concentrations may be modeled as subclasses.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting relative performance variation percent and determined in Fuel Cell Polarization Measurement.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting relative performance variation percent and determined in Fuel Cell Polarization Measurement.
decisions.rationale: The performance observable and comparison convention cannot be recovered from the supplied record.
decisions.implementation: Identify the observable (for example current at a stated voltage, voltage at stated current or peak areal power), test and reference states, and whether the formula is signed relative change, absolute deviation or a symmetric percent difference. Then define the exact numerator and denominator; do not choose peak power without source evidence.

decisions.current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity coefficient low ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The multiplicative prefactor in the low-ionomer-to-carbon-ratio branch of the specified correlation for relative proton conductivity.
decisions.final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity coefficient low ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The contextual record identifies the coefficient role and branch but omits them from the primary definition.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only after attaching source Eq. 7 and defining relative conductivity, R_I/C, the mass basis of R_I/C, the low-ratio domain and the volume-fraction normalization. Do not insert 2.3 as a universal constant or reconstruct the absent equation.

decisions.current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric high for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The exponent applied to the ionomer-to-carbon ratio in the high-ratio branch of the specified relative-proton-conductivity correlation.
decisions.final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric high for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The contextual record identifies which variable is exponentiated and the applicable branch.
decisions.implementation: Attach the complete source correlation, define the R_I/C mass basis and branch threshold, and check whether a shifted ratio rather than R_I/C itself appears in the power before adopting.

decisions.current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric low for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The exponent applied to the ionomer-to-carbon ratio in the low-ratio branch of the specified relative-proton-conductivity correlation.
decisions.final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric low for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The contextual record identifies the exponent role but the primary definition omits it.
decisions.implementation: Attach source Eq. 7, define the R_I/C mass basis and low-ratio regime, and verify the powered expression before adopting.

decisions.current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent vcb for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The exponent applied to the carbon volume fraction in the specified correlation for relative proton conductivity.
decisions.final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent vcb for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The contextual record identifies the powered variable without requiring a guessed numerical exponent.
decisions.implementation: Attach the full source equation and define whether carbon volume fraction is referenced to the entire layer, solid phase or another volume. Check applicability in both correlation branches.

decisions.current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity threshold ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The ionomer-to-carbon ratio at the boundary between the low-ratio and high-ratio branches of a specified relative-proton-conductivity correlation.
decisions.final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity threshold ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The contextual record identifies a branch boundary rather than a generic unspecified threshold.
decisions.implementation: Attach the source correlation, define the R_I/C mass basis and morphology assumptions, and state which branch includes equality. Do not equate this empirical boundary with a universal physical percolation threshold.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting relative volatilization rate and determined in Solvent Property Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: The volatilization rate of a specified liquid divided by that of an identified reference liquid measured under the same protocol and environmental conditions.
decisions.final_value: The volatilization rate of a specified liquid divided by that of an identified reference liquid measured under the same protocol and environmental conditions.
decisions.rationale: A relative rate requires an identified reference rate.
decisions.implementation: Record the reference liquid, rate basis and temperature, airflow, humidity and exposed-geometry conditions. The numerical reference need not be 1 unless that convention is used.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents residual rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents residual rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The record does not identify whether the value is a retained mass fraction, optical-signal fraction or temporal rate.
decisions.implementation: Retrieve the ink-stability assay formula: identify the retained/suspended phase or signal, numerator, initial/reference denominator, sampling height and storage time. Rename to residual fraction if it is a dimensionless retention ratio; reserve rate for a time derivative.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents rheological percolation threshold volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The volume fraction of the specified dispersed-solid phase at which a connected structure first satisfies the stated rheological percolation criterion.
decisions.final_value: The volume fraction of the specified dispersed-solid phase at which a connected structure first satisfies the stated rheological percolation criterion.
decisions.rationale: Identifies the compositional control variable and the operational onset.
decisions.implementation: Define the total-mixture volume basis and the onset criterion, such as an explicitly fitted modulus-scaling threshold; do not assume that a G-prime/G-double-prime crossover always defines percolation.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting roughness factor and determined in Cyclic Voltammetry and Optical Microscopy Imaging Measurement.
decisions.recommended_value: The electrochemically active surface area of the specified electrode material divided by the projected geometric electrode area.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting roughness factor and determined in Cyclic Voltammetry and Optical Microscopy Imaging Measurement.
decisions.rationale: Supplies a conventional electrochemical area-ratio meaning with an explicit numerator and denominator.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only for the CV-derived electrochemical roughness factor. A microscopy-derived topographic real-area/projected-area ratio is a distinct measurement and should use the alternative. Remove inverse roughness factor as an alias.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents saturated ionomer water content lambda for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The number of moles of water per mole of ion-exchange sites in an ionomer at the specified water-saturation equilibrium and temperature.
decisions.final_value: The number of moles of water per mole of ion-exchange sites in an ionomer at the specified water-saturation equilibrium and temperature.
decisions.rationale: Defines lambda using its conventional water-to-site amount ratio.
decisions.implementation: State the ionomer equivalent weight and counterion state and whether saturation is equilibrium with liquid water, ice or saturated water vapor; this is especially important below 0 degrees Celsius.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent a for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The exponent A describing the dependence of plateau storage modulus G0-prime on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation G0-prime proportional to phi raised to A in the specified rheological regime.
decisions.final_value: The exponent A describing the dependence of plateau storage modulus G0-prime on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation G0-prime proportional to phi raised to A in the specified rheological regime.
decisions.rationale: The source description supplies the defining proportionality.
decisions.implementation: Attach source Eq. 5 and specify how G0-prime, phi and the fitted concentration interval are determined; do not transfer A between models without checking the relation.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent b for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The exponent B describing the dependence of the source-defined characteristic strain gamma0 on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation gamma0 proportional to phi raised to B.
decisions.final_value: The exponent B describing the dependence of the source-defined characteristic strain gamma0 on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation gamma0 proportional to phi raised to B.
decisions.rationale: The source description supplies the defining proportionality.
decisions.implementation: Attach source Eq. 6 and identify the operational characteristic-strain criterion and applicable concentration regime.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent t for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The exponent of the excess conducting-phase volume fraction above the specified electrical percolation threshold in a stated power-law correlation for electrical conductivity.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent t for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The supplied equation identifies a percolation conductivity exponent.
decisions.implementation: Confirm that Sigma denotes electrical conductivity in source Eq. 10; state the dispersed conductive-phase volume basis and fitted interval. If Sigma denotes another response, substitute that exact response before adopting.

decisions.current_value: A count characteristic that represents screen mesh count for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The number of mesh threads counted along a specified unit length of a printing screen in a stated mesh direction.
decisions.final_value: The number of mesh threads counted along a specified unit length of a printing screen in a stated mesh direction.
decisions.rationale: Screen mesh count is conventionally a linear thread density.
decisions.implementation: Record threads per centimetre or threads per inch and warp/weft direction. If the source counts openings instead, change threads to openings explicitly; do not treat the two conventions as automatically identical.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents screen volume for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The free volume of a printing-screen mesh available for ink transfer divided by the projected screen area to which that volume refers.
decisions.final_value: The free volume of a printing-screen mesh available for ink transfer divided by the projected screen area to which that volume refers.
decisions.rationale: The description identifies volume per area rather than an absolute volume.
decisions.implementation: Prefer label screen free volume per area; confirm the source meaning and numerical definition of BCM/cm2 before unit conversion, and distinguish mesh free volume from the actual transferred ink volume.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents si c fiber volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The volume occupied by silicon-carbide fibers divided by the total wet formulation volume, multiplied by 100.
decisions.final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents si c fiber volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Defines one explicit constituent-fraction basis rather than leaving the denominator unspecified.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only if the source percentage uses wet formulation volume. If the source uses dry solids or final composite volume, choose the corresponding alternative and narrow the label. Do not merge percentages on different bases.

decisions.current_value: A temporal characteristic that represents simulation time step count for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The number of numerical integration time steps executed in a simulation run.
decisions.final_value: The number of numerical integration time steps executed in a simulation run.
decisions.rationale: Separates a discrete count from simulated duration.
decisions.implementation: Store the integration step duration separately; elapsed simulated time equals the sum of step durations, not necessarily the count times one fixed step when adaptive stepping is used.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents sliding window size for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The number of consecutive past observations or time steps included in the input window of a specified sequence model.
decisions.final_value: The number of consecutive past observations or time steps included in the input window of a specified sequence model.
decisions.rationale: The source context identifies a discrete sequence length.
decisions.implementation: Record sampling interval, missing-data handling and feature count separately; a count alone does not specify a physical window duration.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents smp 10 volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The volume of the identified SMP10 precursor divided by the total wet formulation volume, multiplied by 100.
decisions.final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents smp 10 volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Defines a compositional percentage on one explicit basis.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only after verifying that the source uses total wet formulation volume. Record the exact precursor product and whether volumes are summed dispensed-component volumes or measured final mixture volumes. If solvent-free volume is intended, use the alternative.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents solid content fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The total mass of dry solid constituents in an ink divided by the total mass of the wet ink.
decisions.final_value: A composition characteristic that represents solid content fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: Gives the conventional gravimetric solids-content meaning and distinguishes it from solids volume fraction.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only if the source uses a mass basis. Define which components count as dry solids, including whether ionomer/binder is included and the drying criterion. For volume fraction, use the separately defined SolidLoadingVolumeFraction.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents solid loading volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The volume occupied by the specified solid constituents divided by the total volume of the wet ink formulation.
decisions.final_value: The volume occupied by the specified solid constituents divided by the total volume of the wet ink formulation.
decisions.rationale: Identifies the phase-volume numerator and mixture denominator.
decisions.implementation: Record included solids, density assumptions and whether total ink volume is measured or calculated additively. Use a separately identified dry-composite fraction for a dry denominator.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents solvent evaporation rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The rate at which the mass of solvent remaining in the sample decreases, normalized by the initial sample mass.
decisions.final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents solvent evaporation rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.rationale: The contextual description identifies a mass-fraction loss rate, rather than an absolute mass-loss rate or evaporation flux.
decisions.implementation: Adopt only if the paper defines a solvent-loss mass fraction relative to initial sample mass. Then r = -(1/m0) dm_solvent/dt is positive for evaporation. If the denominator is initial solvent mass, use the alternative. If the reported quantity is d(current mass fraction)/dt, recover that exact equation rather than substituting this definition.

decisions.current_value: A composition characteristic that represents solvent to carbon ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The combined mass of the specified ink solvents divided by the mass of carbon support in the same catalyst-ink formulation.
decisions.final_value: The combined mass of the specified ink solvents divided by the mass of carbon support in the same catalyst-ink formulation.
decisions.rationale: The context establishes a solvent-to-carbon mass ratio.
decisions.implementation: State which liquids count as solvents and whether water is included; exclude metal and ionomer from the carbon denominator. Prefer label solvent-to-carbon mass ratio.

decisions.current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents solvent to water volume ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The volume of the identified nonaqueous solvent divided by the volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture.
decisions.final_value: The volume of the identified nonaqueous solvent divided by the volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture.
decisions.rationale: Defines the numerator, denominator and volume basis.
decisions.implementation: State solvent identity and dispensed-volume versus final-component-volume convention; do not treat this ratio as a solvent volume fraction.

decisions.current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents sonication amplitude percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
decisions.recommended_value: The sonotrode oscillation-amplitude setting expressed as a percentage of the maximum amplitude specified for the selected ultrasonic processor, probe and operating configuration.
decisions.final_value: The sonotrode oscillation-amplitude setting expressed as a percentage of the maximum amplitude specified for the selected ultrasonic processor, probe and operating configuration.
decisions.rationale: An amplitude setting is not a percentage of acoustic or electrical power.  References 35, 36.
decisions.implementation: Confirm the instrument documentation and amplitude convention. Remove percent-of-maximum-power aliases; report actual power/energy independently.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting specific activity.
decisions.recommended_value: The kinetic current for a specified electrocatalytic reaction divided by the electrochemically active surface area of the catalyst under stated measurement conditions.
decisions.final_value: A property denoting specific activity.
decisions.rationale: Provides the conventional electrochemical area-specific activity meaning, distinct from mass activity.
decisions.implementation: Adopt for area-specific electrocatalytic activity. Identify reaction, potential/reference electrode, catalyst/ECSA material, current corrections and test conditions. If a source uses another meaning of specific activity, define a separate, explicitly normalized class.

decisions.current_value: A property denoting dimensionless coverage inferred by normalizing CO displacement charge at 0.4 Vcell to ECA.
decisions.recommended_value: The fraction of the specified platinum adsorption sites occupied by sulfonate species under stated electrode and electrolyte conditions.
